question: What evidence is required to compare our Oscilloscope solution with a competitor for Automotive without making unsupported claims?
answer: The Vault contains no oscilloscope product pages (no R&S RTO/RTP/MXO entity notes), no oscilloscope battle card, and no automotive oscilloscope competitive comparison — oscilloscopes appear only as unresolved [[Oscilloscope]] mentions in solution-mapping tables that explicitly note no model or test item is given. What the Vault does document is a transferable evidence standard, set by the three CMX500 battle-card syntheses: a sales battle card is "sales positioning", not binding technical specifications, so every R&S number must be traced to the official specifications / features document with its document number and version. Claims about the competitor coming from a single R&S internal battle card are not usable in customer documents until the competitor's own official datasheet/brochure and independent third-party evidence are obtained. Superlatives — "only platform", "first", "leadership", "fewer boxes", "lower TCO" — are sales language that must either be dropped or backed by a formal datasheet, features document, conformance report or configuration tool; TCO claims specifically need a calculation or empirical data, which the sources do not provide. PR and demonstration material counts only as demonstration-level evidence and must carry test conditions (bandwidth, throughput, MCS index, software version, measurement uncertainty) before it is used as a spec. For the Automotive dimension the Vault's only comparable precedent is NG eCall: a compliance claim needs the named standard and version (EN 17240:2024), test case IDs, test conditions, setup and software versions and pass/fail details, and must not upgrade "verification" into formal third-party "certification". Applying that standard to an Oscilloscope-vs-competitor Automotive comparison is not possible from this Vault, because none of the required product-level or competitor-level documents exist here.
missing: The Vault has no R&S oscilloscope product pages (no RTO/RTP/MXO entity notes, datasheet or specifications document), no oscilloscope sales battle card, no named oscilloscope competitor pages, and no automotive oscilloscope test-requirement or standards content (e.g. automotive Ethernet/CAN/SerDes/power-rail test specs). It therefore lacks the R&S-side official specification numbers, the competitor-side official datasheets, any third-party or conformance reports, automotive standard/test-case references, and any TCO calculation that its own evidence rules would demand for such a comparison. Only the generic competitive-claim methodology (from the CMX500 vs Keysight/Anritsu/amarisoft syntheses) and the NG eCall automotive verification precedent are available.

key_points.point: A sales battle card is sales positioning, not binding technical specifications — R&S figures must be traced to the official specs/features documents instead
key_points.quote: 其性質是 sales positioning，不是 binding technical specifications。

key_points.point: Superlative/positioning statements cannot be used as verifiable specifications; they must be checked back against a formal datasheet, features document, conformance report or configuration tool
key_points.quote: 不能當作可驗證規格，需回查正式 datasheet、features document、conformance report 或配置工具。

key_points.point: Competitor claims resting on a single R&S internal battle card require the competitor's own official data plus third-party evidence before use in customer-facing documents
key_points.quote: 若用於客戶文件，應另查 Keysight 官方資料與第三方證據。

key_points.point: Phrases such as "only platform", "industry-leading", "widest" and "lower TCO" are sales language and must not be treated as verifiable technical specifications
key_points.quote: Source 中的 only platform、industry-leading、widest frequency range、lower TCO 等語句是 sales language，不應當作可驗證技術規格。

key_points.point: Cost/TCO advantage claims need a calculation or empirical data, which the battle-card sources do not supply
key_points.quote: TCO 未有算式或實證資料

key_points.point: Press-release or demo evidence counts only as demonstration-level evidence unless test conditions, software version and measurement uncertainty are given
